cross_references.relationship: federal counterpart — §1347 applies to health care benefit programs affecting commerce (Medicare Advantage contracts); §550 applies to all California-regulated insurers. Both apply to Blue Shield. §550 is easier to establish — no interstate commerce requirement. §1347 carries heavier penalties and federal investigative resources.

administrative predicate — §10123.135 violation (non-physician UR, AI denial) creates the record of insurer misconduct; §550(b)(1) applies if the denial letter contained false statements about the review conducted. A §10123.135 violation does not automatically constitute §550 fraud, but a denial letter falsely claiming physician review when none occurred IS a §550(b)(1) violation.

procedural companion — exhausting IMR (§1374.30) is required before certain claims; an insurer that denies IMR access or provides false records to the IMR organization commits a separate §550(b)(1) violation
